mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.0% indicates an accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 4.0% but 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a tightening labor market that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 3.5% but 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 5.0%) and accommodative monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 4.5%) signals stagflationary risks that depress equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 5.0% and FEDFUNDS < 4.5% but 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (characterized by strong GDP growth and low unemployment), a decline in housing starts below 1300 thousand units signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0% and UNRATE < 3.5%), HOUST below 1300 thousand units is followed by positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production above 102.0 signals robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO above 102.0 but 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL reading above 5.0% signals persistent inflation that may prompt aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 5.0% but 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 100k) and weak retail sales (RSAFS < 700k) signals an economy with excess labor supply relative to consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS > 100k and RSAFS < 700k but 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During recessions (defined by GDPC1 growth < 0.0% annualized), a rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% signals worsening economic conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In recession regimes (GDPC1 growth < 0.0% annualized), UNRATE rise above 4.0% is followed by positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances.
